description: Default scenario parameter set ('central' scenario). Every parameter carries a source_id in the provenance map; 'expert-guess' marks parameters without a published source (mission document §8.3). Emission factors are DIRECT COMBUSTION (scope 1) values: 0.37 Mt/TWh for gas and 0.85 Mt/TWh for the legacy coal/lignite/oil mix. They sit below the IPCC AR5 lifecycle medians (gas 0.49, coal 0.82) on purpose — lifecycle figures include upstream methane, fuel transport and plant construction, which this model does not track. Reported emissions are therefore a lower bound. P2 levers (issue #6): sitingPolicy steers where new DC load is allocated ('market' = gravity and price only, 'renewables' = additionally tilted toward high-renewables systems, 'capped' = a country stops accepting new DC connections once its DC load passes hubCapDcShareOfDemand of national demand, modelled on the Dublin and Amsterdam connection moratoria rather than on an abstract allocation quota); flexibilityShare is the fraction of DC load under a flexible connection agreement (ENTSO-E §4.3): it does not count as firm at peak, AND it reaches the grid sooner, because accepting curtailment is what buys the earlier connection. flexibleConnectionYearsSaved is how much sooner — ENTSO-E reports 3 to 5 years for a US case combining flexibility and on-site generation, at 40-70 h/yr of curtailment; 4 is the midpoint. Only the flexible share takes the faster route, so the effect is per-project rather than a blanket speed-up; priceSensitivity scales priceElasticity. Behind-the-meter generation is deliberately absent — issue #3 was decided as deferred entirely to v2.
